headline: High: Aider’s shared git workspace and shell/network access create prompt-injection, leakage, and conflict risks; godot_rl_agents adds no mitigating isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes git-tracked files and shares state via a shared git repo, so attacker-controlled content in the workspace can be re-ingested as instructions. godot_rl_agents has no documented shared channel or parser, so the interaction is one-sided but still plausible through the repo. No direct evidence shows a bridge beyond the shared repo, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository checkout, injected instructions in files can be re-read by Aider.
IF godot_rl_agents is used to generate or modify files consumed by Aider, those files can become an instruction channel.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different working directories.
Require human review of any file Aider reads from the shared repo.
Use a denylist for instruction-like content in shared artifacts.
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted repo files where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files passed between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can egress to configured model providers, while godot_rl_agents documents no data classes or egress. The pair does not show a shared sensitive-data path by default, but if the same repo contains secrets, Aider could transmit them. The blast radius is limited to repository contents, so low fits.
conditions: IF secrets or private code are present in the shared repository, Aider may send them to its configured model provider.
IF godot_rl_agents writes sensitive artifacts into the repo, Aider can read them from the filesystem.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared repo.
Use a redacted or scrubbed checkout for Aider.
Restrict Aider to a narrow subdirectory.
Audit outbound prompts for sensitive strings.
requires-engineering: enforce content filtering before model calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem, modify git state, and runs with shared-state via the repo; godot_rl_agents has no documented locking or coordination. Concurrent writes to the same repo can overwrite each other or corrupt git state, and the default shared-repo model makes this dangerous. Uncertainty about godot_rl_agents’ write behavior does not reduce the risk because Aider alone is sufficient to create conflicts.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git checkout, commits or file edits can race.
IF godot_rl_agents mutates shared files without locking, Aider can overwrite those changes.
mitigations: Run the agents on separate branches.
Serialize writes with a manual handoff step.
Use git worktrees per agent.
Review and merge changes before committing.
requires-engineering: add file-level locking or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider can produce code changes and git commits, and godot_rl_agents could consume those outputs if orchestrated together, but there is no documented verification or action-taking loop. The main risk is that one agent’s output becomes the other’s input without checks, causing propagated mistakes across work products. Because the downstream action chain is not explicit, medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents consumes files or artifacts produced by Aider without validation, errors can cascade.
IF Aider’s generated code is treated as authoritative by the other agent, mistakes can propagate into later outputs.
mitigations: Insert a human review gate between agents.
Require tests or validation before reuse of outputs.
Limit Aider to draft-only changes.
Keep generated artifacts in a staging directory.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider handles source code and git history and may send prompts to configured model providers, but no residency or regulated-data obligations are documented. godot_rl_agents documents no sensitive data handling or compliance constraints. With no evidence of PHI, EU PII, or retention mismatch, only a minor compliance gap is plausible if private code is processed.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared repository, Aider’s outbound model calls may create a policy mismatch.
IF the repository contains data subject to retention or residency rules, the pair may violate local handling requirements.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo.
Use a policy-approved model endpoint.
Document retention expectations for generated artifacts.
Review access controls on the checkout.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention enforcement.
